lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Verify that the profile URL is real and professional, and replace it if it is a placeholder.
items.because: “example.com” may be only a placeholder.

items.says: Label the profile as LinkedIn if it is a LinkedIn URL.
Use an email address you monitor regularly.
Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is unnecessary for most U.S. applications and may introduce discrimination concerns.

items.says: Remove the nationality.
items.because: It is generally unnecessary; work authorization can be addressed separately if needed.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or expected.
items.because: The date may make an ongoing degree look completed.

items.says: Add a concentration only if it is relevant to the targeted product-management roles.
Add GPA, honors, or coursework only if they strengthen the candidacy.
Make the B.A. abbreviation consistent with the MBA formatting.
Optionally identify the internship as an MBA internship if relevant.
Define what “conversion” measures.
items.because: It could refer to different stages of the payments funnel.

items.says: Specify the comparison period or baseline for the 35% increase.
items.because: The metric’s validity is unclear without it.

items.says: Verify “for all merchants” or state the actual rollout or pilot scope.
items.because: A universal rollout claim may invite scrutiny.

items.says: Say whether the increase came from an experiment or a before-and-after comparison.
items.because: The measurement method is unclear.

items.says: Distinguish the checkout initiative from the merchant-onboarding initiative.
items.because: The bullets appear overlapping or potentially duplicative.

items.says: Specify whether you independently authored, led, or contributed to the requirements.
items.because: Your level of ownership is unclear.

items.says: Add a post-launch customer or business outcome if one exists.
items.because: The result focuses on schedule rather than the feature’s impact.

items.says: Clarify the relationship between your work and the early launch.
items.because: The wording could imply you alone caused the schedule improvement.

items.says: Use U.S.-consistent spelling instead of “analysed.”
items.because: The résumé otherwise appears aimed at a U.S. audience.

items.says: Clarify whether $1.1 million is an estimate, annualized exposure, or actual annual losses.
items.because: The calculation needs greater precision.

items.says: Format the currency consistently and identify it if ambiguous.
Separate the research, quantified finding, and roadmap consequence more clearly.
items.because: The decision-making process needs greater precision.

items.says: Clarify your role rather than implying the business case alone set the roadmap priority.
items.because: The decision-making process is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether you closed the tickets or coordinated the team that did.
items.because: The scope of your responsibility is unclear.

items.says: Define the comparison point for cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
items.because: The basis for “by half” is unclear.

items.says: Distinguish product issues from customer-support requests if possible.
items.because: The scope of the tickets is unclear.

items.says: Add the measurement finding, not just the method.
items.because: The bullet describes a process rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Name the metric compared and the decision or conclusion that resulted.
items.because: The result of the comparison is missing.

items.says: Acknowledge that the opt-in comparison was non-random if relevant.
items.because: Self-selected groups are not necessarily comparable.

items.says: Clarify whether you led, designed, or supported the redesign.
items.because: Your role is unclear.

items.says: Explain how this result relates to the preceding measurement bullet.
items.because: The relationship between the bullets is unclear.

items.says: Identify whether the result used a comparable control group or a before-and-after baseline.
items.because: How the improvement was measured is unclear.

items.says: Ensure the sample and measurement period are defensible.
items.because: The quantified impact needs measurement context.

items.says: Distinguish this onboarding initiative from the checkout initiative.
items.because: Together, the bullets leave uncertainty about how many separate initiatives you owned.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the on-time calculation rather than necessarily cutting late deliveries.
items.because: It may look like manipulating the metric instead of improving delivery performance.

items.says: Give separate evidence if operational delivery performance also improved.
items.because: The revised calculation does not establish that improvement.

items.says: Explain the business or reporting purpose of the revised calculation.
items.because: The current presentation could undermine credibility.

items.says: Consider adding “by” before “30%.”
items.because: It may improve grammatical clarity.

items.says: Clarify the baseline or time period for the error reduction.
items.because: Additional context would make the impact more credible.

items.says: Specify whether you led the redesign, analyzed the problem, or coordinated implementation.
items.because: Your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Add the operational or financial impact of fewer errors if available.
items.because: It would make the impact more concrete.

items.says: “Prepares” is present tense in a role that ended in 2023.
items.because: It is inconsistent with the past-tense bullet and other past-role bullets.

items.says: Use list punctuation consistently.
items.because: The résumé should follow one convention for serial commas.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned the forecast, compiled inputs, or managed the review.
items.because: The nature of your responsibility is unclear.

items.says: Add an outcome if available.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities rather than demonstrated impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the tool was implemented at all three depots.
items.because: The rollout scope is unclear.

items.says: State whether the annual savings were measured or projected.
items.because: The savings calculation should be defensible.

items.says: Describe your implementation role beyond training if applicable.
items.because: Your contribution to the rollout is unclear.

items.says: Define whether “driver hours” means paid hours, scheduled hours, or estimated route time.
items.because: The savings measure is ambiguous.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” is accurate.
Identify the project clearly as an ongoing extracurricular or venture project.
items.because: It overlaps with the MBA and Harbor internship.

items.says: Consider giving the Campus Food Rescue project less space relative to professional experience.
items.because: The final résumé length should remain concise.

items.says: Use a measurement system consistent with the résumé’s geography and audience.
items.because: “Tonnes” may not align with them.

items.because: The adoption figure needs precision.

items.says: Distinguish food made available from food actually redistributed if they differ.
items.because: The food-volume claim needs precision.

items.says: Confirm that the first-year result is complete and measured.
items.because: The project is marked ongoing.

items.says: Clarify whether reminders caused the user growth or merely preceded it.
items.because: The causal claim needs stronger evidence.

items.says: Give the relevant time frame and, if available, a comparison with users who received no reminders.
items.because: That would strengthen the causal claim.

items.says: Define whether weekly active users covers the whole product or the reminder-exposed group.
items.because: The metric’s population is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed the system, recruited volunteers, managed scheduling, or did all three.
items.because: Your ownership is unclear.

items.says: Explain whether fewer staff cover shifts directly resulted from the system and whether service quality held up.
items.because: The operational result needs context.

items.says: Ensure the percentages and counts use a consistent weekly measurement period.
items.because: The measurements need to be comparable.

items.says: Check whether the client can be named publicly; otherwise use a confidentiality-safe description.
items.because: The client’s identity may be confidential.

items.because: The network scope is unclear.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to mapping and redesigning intake.

items.because: “Shortened” is less persuasive without a measurable result.

items.says: State whether adoption was informal, leadership-approved, or standard process.
items.because: “Adopted” lacks implementation context.

items.says: Add a patient, staff, or throughput outcome if available.

Order the Harbor bullets by relevance and strength, and group related onboarding bullets.
